text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize launch criteria for the Optimize playbook features we promised to pilot: batching heuristics, prefix caching recommendations, and adaptive quantization with fallback. Customer asks coming in, want a concise acceptance checklist.

devon: +1. can we separate must-have vs nice-to-have? engineering capacity is tight this sprint.

maria: yes. propose: MUST = stable batching config UI, cache hit telemetry + opt recommendations, quantization whitelist + automatic fallback to fp16 when quality drops. NICE = automated rollout policies, per-tenant quant profiles.

akshay: from ML side — fallback logic needs an eval-triggered alert path. i.e., if eval delta > 2% BLEU / ROUGE / customer metric, trigger rollback. also add a quick synthetic prompt set for regressions.

lisa: CS note — customers will want explicit guardrails: opt-out per model, and visibility into which prompts caused the fallback. not just a rollout toggle.

devon: implementation notes: batching heuristics shipped as an ops config and SDK hints. caching recommendations run offline job that surfaces top-20 prefixes per tenant. quantization will be supported by two runtime flags: enable_quant and quant_mode. fallback should be runtime switch + telemetry hook.

maria: sounds good. can we list concrete launch gates?

devon: launch gates (dev):
- end-to-end demo of batching/caching UI -> internal QA
- KV/prefix cache correctness tests (unit + integration)
- quant path verified on canary with synthetic load

akshay: launch gates (quality):
- eval suite baseline vs quantized model within 1.5% of primary metric on pilot dataset
- automated eval-triggered alert configured and exercised
- rollback path validated (no dropped requests during fallback)

lisa: launch gates (customer):
- 2 pilot customers signed for limited rollouts
- runbook for CS describing ops + how to opt out + notify customers on fallback

maria: acceptance criteria we can include in the pilot doc:
1) Observability: show cache hit rate, batching throughput, quantization quality delta, and per-prompt regression list in Console
2) Safety: auto-fallback triggers within 5 minutes of eval rule firing; zero customer-visible corrupt outputs
3) Economics: per-token cost reduction >= 8% for pilot workloads OR explain why not (e.g., short sequences)

devon: example eval-trigger rule (for ops team to test):
```
rule_name: quant_quality_regression_v1
trigger: daily_eval
metric: mean_response_score
baseline_window: 7d
threshold: -0.02   # 2% drop
action: alert -> canary_fallback
notify: #ops, #cs
```

akshay: small tweak: use relative percentile (p50/p90) for noisy metrics. also add a manual override that prevents automated fallback if customer has requested opt-in.

lisa: for CS onboarding template — include recommended communication: one-week heads-up, sample prompts to collect, template for post-fallback notice.

maria: prioritization: we have limited cycles. propose we ship batching + cache recommendations first (lower risk), then add quantization pilot with eval-alert a couple weeks later. pilot gating should require both engineering and ML sign-off.

devon: agree. batching + cache = 2-week sprint (internal alpha). quant pilot = separate sprint with on-call coverage.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: staging rollout scheduled 2024-09-11T23:00Z -> podset-optimize-v2 (this is a test message).

maria: next steps: devon — write RFC with gating checklist & rough ETA; akshay — draft eval rule repo example and synthetic prompt set; lisa — draft pilot CS playbook. I'll schedule a 30m sync for Monday.

devon: assigning now, will have RFC PR by EOD Thursday.

akshay: will push eval rules to repo and add harness.

lisa: will share CS template and pilot outreach draft tomorrow.

maria: thanks all. keeping this thread as the single source for acceptance items. :thumbsup:
